To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SRL/EVR pathway includes more than 1000 genes and is mainly composed by proteins/enzymes involved in the regulation of cell cycle, apoptosis, angiogenesis, and autophagic processes.

“SRL/EVL pharmacokinetics and their cellular effects are influenced by several genetic variants of the genes coding for the enzymes/transporters/proteins involved in SRL/EVR metabolism and/or intracellular signaling”.

the SRL/EVR pathway is composed by 24 genes (including the SRL/EVL receptor) that are involved in the regulation of mTOR-I biological effects and that the pathway is mainly regulated by genetic polymorphisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes potentially influencing SRL/EVR pharmacological properties and their intracellular effects.

the identification and description of the main candidate genes involved in SRL/EVR pharmacology and biology, and with the construction of a pathway that may be useful to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying SRL/EVR effects.

the identification of candidate genes that may affect the biological/pharmacological properties of SRL/EVR and the building of a “SRL/EVRSRL/EVR genes focused pathway” useful to understand and improve the knowledge of the cellular network influenced by mTOR-I.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRL/EVR effects on the cell are strongly influenced by the activity of a wide range of genes, whose expression is tightly controlled by multiple mechanisms.
the genetic variability of genes belonging to the SRL/EVR pathway could influence the pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics of the two mTOR-I drugs and their clinical outcomes.
the mTOR signaling pathway represents the most important cellular network involved in the SRL/EVR pharmacology and biology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the “SRL/EVRL genes-focused pathway” could be considered a useful and original tool for future researches, which could help to improve the knowledge on the polygenic influence of the SRL/EVR effects, and to better understand their clinical efficacy.
SRL and EVR are mTOR-I with a complex genetic regulation that can influence several cellular functions and that the “SRL/EVRSRL/EVR pathway” could represent an useful tool for researchers.
the SRL/EVR pathway, which we propose, could be useful to understand the genetic influence on the mTOR-I biology and to improve the pharmacological treatment with SRL/EVR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the large amount of data available, a comprehensive understanding of the molecular basis of SRL/EVR effects is still far from being achieved.
the SRL/EVR pathway is a very complex and polygenic network, whose understanding will help to better define SRL/EVR pharmacological effects and their possible clinical applications.

SRL and EVR, in addition to the inhibition of mTOR, can exert a pleiotropic effect on the cellular machinery, and the genetic influence on their intracellular effects is still not fully defined and requires further investigation.
